text: {"score":2,"justification":"Core numbers match the card (17.6% vs 4.3%, 272 claims, z 2.30, score 4.03, 0 documented). But the narrative has unsupported or contradictory content, and the headline and text lack grounding. The headline claims 'the office objected to the scope and then did not respond' and the text says 'I closed the request as non-responsive'; neither appears in the packet (it only shows 0 documented claims). The statement 'moderate and spread across complexity levels' conflicts with the card: ratio is 4.13x, z 2.3, and 99215 share rises to 55.6% in the 5+ condition group, so the elevation is concentrated in high-complexity patients, though low-complexity share is still 7-8%. The summary does not use the high-complexity evidence or the 55.6% figure, and two examples are only a sample of seven low-complexity claims. Next steps are generic and vaguely worded ('larger sample'), with no specific claims to request. The cautious tone on non-response is good, and the missing documentation is flagged.","problems":["Headline asserts the office objected to scope and did not respond; no support in the evidence packet","'I closed the request as non-responsive' is an unsupported process claim","'Moderate and spread across complexity levels' mischaracterizes the card (4.13x expected, concentrated at 5+ conditions at 55.6%)","No complexity-banded numbers given, so billed level vs patient complexity is only thinly explained (only 15% low-complexity share)","Only two cited low-complexity examples; no high-complexity contrast, and the 99214 comparators are ignored","Next steps are generic: no specific claim IDs to request documentation for","'Re-screen once records arrive' is vague and contradicts the idea that records were already requested and not returned"]}
